config.title: border-radius and box-shadow

intro.title: border-radius and box-shadow
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a visually appealing card component with rounded corners and a subtle shadow to make it stand out. You will learn how to use the CSS border-radius property to create smooth, rounded edges on elements. You will also apply the box-shadow property to add depth and dimension to your card, making it look like it's floating above the page. This lesson focuses on these two fundamental CSS properties to enhance the style and modern feel of web elements.
intro.usecase: The border-radius and box-shadow properties are essential for creating modern, visually appealing UI components that users interact with daily. You'll use border-radius to create rounded corners on buttons, cards, and profile avatars in social media apps and e-commerce sites. Box-shadow adds depth and dimension to interactive elements like modal dialogs, form inputs, and notification panels in dashboards and web applications. Together, these properties help distinguish clickable elements from static content, improve visual hierarchy, and create polished interfaces that feel tactile and responsive.

objectives: Apply border-radius to create rounded corners on HTML elements
Configure box-shadow properties to add depth and dimension to elements
Manipulate border-radius values to create different corner rounding effects
Construct layered shadow effects using multiple box-shadow declarations
Integrate border-radius and box-shadow to style interactive button components
Control the spread and blur radius of box-shadow for precise shadow effects
Implement elliptical corners by specifying horizontal and vertical border-radius values

steps.title: Create a CSS file and add a basic HTML structure reference
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS file and add a comment at the top showing the HTML structure we'll be styling with border-radius and box-shadow.
steps.hint: Start with a CSS comment that describes the HTML elements you'll be styling. This helps keep your CSS organized.
steps.analogousExample:
/* HTML structure we'll style:

Card Title

Card content goes here.

*/
steps.expectedOutcome: A CSS file is created with a comment showing the HTML structure that will receive border-radius and box-shadow styling.
successCriteria: The CSS file contains a comment describing the HTML elements to be styled.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created the CSS file, but make sure to include a comment describing the HTML elements you'll be styling. Add a comment like the example to show the structure.
steps.feedbackWrong: It looks like the CSS file doesn't have the required comment. Create a CSS file and add a comment at the top showing the HTML structure we'll style with border-radius and box-shadow.

steps.title: Create a basic box element style
steps.instruction: Define a CSS class named .box with the following properties: width: 200px, height: 200px, background-color: #f0f0f0, and margin: 20px auto.
steps.hint: Start with .box { } and add each property inside the curly braces, separated by semicolons.
steps.expectedOutcome: A .box class is defined with the specified width, height, background color, and margin properties.
successCriteria: The .box class exists and contains width: 200px, height: 200px, background-color: #f0f0f0, and margin: 20px auto.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but some properties are missing or incorrect. Make sure your .box class has all four required properties with the exact values specified.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .box class is not properly defined. Check that you've spelled the class name correctly (.box) and included all four properties with their values inside curly braces.

steps.title: Add border-radius property to create rounded corners
steps.instruction: Inside the .box class, add the border-radius property with a value of 10px to create slightly rounded corners.
steps.hint: Add 'border-radius: 10px;' to the .box selector to round all four corners equally.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have rounded corners with a 10px radius.
successCriteria: The .box class contains the border-radius property set to 10px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added 'border-radius: 10px;' inside the .box selector.
steps.feedbackWrong: The border-radius property wasn't added correctly. Check that you've placed 'border-radius: 10px;' inside the .box class.

steps.title: Experiment with different border-radius values
steps.instruction: Change the border-radius value from 10px to 25px to create more rounded corners.
steps.hint: Look for the border-radius property in the .box selector and replace the current value with 25px.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have more noticeably rounded corners.
successCriteria: The border-radius property for .box is set to 25px.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're changing the border-radius value to exactly 25px.
steps.feedbackWrong: The border-radius value wasn't updated correctly. Check that you changed it to 25px.

steps.title: Add box-shadow property for basic shadow
steps.instruction: Add a box-shadow property to the .box selector to create a subtle shadow effect. Use the values: 5px horizontal offset, 5px vertical offset, 10px blur radius, and rgba(0,0,0,0.3) for the color with transparency.
steps.hint: The box-shadow property takes multiple values: horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color. Add it after the border-radius property in your .box rule.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have a subtle shadow appearing slightly offset to the bottom-right with a soft blur.
successCriteria: The .box selector includes a box-shadow property with the exact values: 5px 5px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.3).
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Check that your box-shadow property has all four values in the correct order: horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color.
steps.feedbackWrong: The box-shadow property is missing or incorrect. Review the instruction and add the property with the specified values.

steps.title: Understand box-shadow syntax components
steps.instruction: Add a CSS comment above the box-shadow property explaining each component: horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color.
steps.hint: Write a comment like /* horizontal vertical blur color */ above the box-shadow line.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example comment explaining CSS property */
color: blue;
steps.expectedOutcome: The learner will understand the four components of the box-shadow property by adding a descriptive comment.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is added above the box-shadow property explaining horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but make sure it mentions all four components: horizontal offset, vertical offset, blur radius, and color.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a CSS comment above the box-shadow property that explains each component value.

steps.title: Create an inset shadow effect
steps.instruction: Modify the existing box-shadow property to create an inner shadow by adding the 'inset' keyword at the beginning of the value.
steps.hint: Add the word 'inset' before the existing shadow values in your box-shadow property.
steps.analogousExample:
/* Example of an inset shadow */
box-shadow: inset 2px 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,0.2);
steps.expectedOutcome: The box will now display a shadow that appears inside the element, creating a recessed or pressed effect.
successCriteria: The box-shadow property includes the 'inset' keyword before the shadow values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added the 'inset' keyword at the beginning of the box-shadow value.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check your box-shadow property. It should start with 'inset' followed by the shadow values.

steps.title: Combine multiple shadows
steps.instruction: Add a second shadow to the .box element to create a more complex effect by separating multiple shadows with commas. Use: box-shadow: 5px 5px 10px rgba(0,0,0,0.3), inset 2px 2px 5px rgba(255,255,255,0.5);
steps.hint: You can apply multiple shadows to one element by listing them separated by commas in the box-shadow property. The first shadow is already there; add a comma and the second shadow.
steps.expectedOutcome: The .box element will have both an outer shadow and an inner (inset) shadow, creating a more dimensional effect.
successCriteria: The .box selector has a box-shadow property with two comma-separated values: the existing outer shadow and a new inset shadow.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you have two shadows separated by a comma in the box-shadow property.
steps.feedbackWrong: Check that you've added a second shadow value after a comma in the box-shadow property.

steps.title: Create a second styled element with different properties
steps.instruction: Create a new CSS class called .card with different border-radius and box-shadow values.
steps.hint: Define a new CSS rule starting with .card { } and add border-radius and box-shadow properties inside.
steps.expectedOutcome: A new .card CSS class with distinct border-radius and box-shadow values.
successCriteria: The .card class is defined with both border-radius and box-shadow properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You created the .card class, but it's missing either border-radius or box-shadow properties.
steps.feedbackWrong: The .card class is not properly defined with both border-radius and box-shadow properties.

steps.title: Review and compare both styled elements
steps.instruction: Add a CSS comment above the .card class that describes how its border-radius and box-shadow differ from the .box class.
steps.hint: Write a comment like /* This card has... */ to note the visual differences between the two elements.
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a descriptive comment that helps reinforce the differences between the two styled elements.
successCriteria: A CSS comment is added above the .card class that mentions border-radius and box-shadow differences.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a comment, but make sure it specifically mentions how border-radius and/or box-shadow differ between the .box and .card elements.
steps.feedbackWrong: Try adding a CSS comment above the .card class that describes the visual differences in border-radius and box-shadow between the two elements.
